title: State Non-Economic Damage Caps in Personal Injury Cases
note: Laws change frequently. This table reflects 2024 information. Always verify current law with a licensed attorney in your state. Some caps apply only to medical malpractice; others are general. 'None' means no statutory cap — juries may still award any amount.

rows.notes: No statutory cap on non-economic damages; punitive damages capped at $1.5M or 3x compensatory.
Non-economic cap is $400k or 4x compensatory, whichever is greater. Adjusted periodically.
Arizona courts struck down damage caps; no current statutory cap on non-economic damages.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages in personal injury or medical malpractice cases.
MICRA cap increased from $250k in 2023; rises $40k/year until $750k (2033), then indexed to CPI.
Unified cap applies to all personal injury and med mal; adjusted annually for inflation (CPI-W).
No statutory cap. Courts may set aside excessive verdicts under remittitur.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
DC has no non-economic damage cap.
Florida Supreme Court struck down med mal cap in 2017 (Kalitan). Caps technically on the books but constitutionally unenforceable in most cases.
Georgia Supreme Court struck down $350k med mal cap in 2010 (Atlanta Oculoplastic Surgery).
Medical malpractice non-economic damages capped at $375,000.
Med mal non-economic cap indexed to inflation; approximately $415k as of 2024.
Illinois Supreme Court struck down $500k/$1M caps in 2010 (Lebron v. Gottlieb). No current cap.
Total med mal recovery (economic + non-economic) capped at $1.8M; providers pay first $500k.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
Non-economic med mal cap started at $250k (1988), adjusted for inflation; ~$325k as of 2024.
No statutory cap; Kentucky courts have rejected damage caps as unconstitutional.
Total med mal recovery (incl. future medical) capped at $500k above a $100k patient compensation fund.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
Cap increases $15k/year; applies to all wrongful death and personal injury med mal claims.
No statutory cap; punitive damages limited to egregious conduct.
Non-economic med mal cap indexed to CPI; higher threshold ($824,200) for death/permanent serious injury.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
Non-economic med mal cap of $500k. General personal injury cases have no cap.
Med mal non-economic cap reinstated at $400k (catastrophic injury $700k) after 2015 amendment.
Montana Supreme Court struck down $250k cap as unconstitutional. No current cap.
Total recovery cap (economic + non-economic combined) for med mal cases.
Non-economic med mal cap of $350k. No general personal injury cap.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
No statutory cap; courts use remittitur to address excessive verdicts.
Total med mal recovery cap (excluding future medical); adjusted periodically by legislature.
No statutory cap. NY courts frequently reduce excessive verdicts via remittitur.
Non-economic med mal cap indexed to CPI from 2011 base of $500k; ~$600k+ as of 2024.
Non-economic med mal damages capped at $500,000.
Non-economic cap $350k per person / $500k per occurrence; $500k for catastrophic injury. Applies broadly.
Non-economic med mal cap of $350k reinstated by statute after earlier court challenges.
Non-economic med mal damages capped at $500,000.
No statutory cap; Pennsylvania courts rely on remittitur for excessive verdicts.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
Non-economic med mal cap per defendant is $350k; aggregate $1.05M for all defendants. Adjusted periodically.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
Non-economic cap of $750k applies broadly; $1M for catastrophic injury. Applies to personal injury and med mal.
Multi-tiered med mal cap: $250k per physician, $250k per health care institution, max $500k from institutions.
Non-economic med mal cap of $450,000.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
Total med mal recovery cap (economic + non-economic) indexed annually; increasing to $3M by 2031.
Washington Supreme Court struck down med mal cap. No current statutory cap.
Non-economic med mal cap of $300k per occurrence. Legislature has repeatedly revisited this limit.
Non-economic med mal cap of $750k. Wisconsin Supreme Court upheld constitutionality in 2018.
No statutory cap on non-economic damages.
